title: Ultrasound imaging of placental vascular anastomoses using Slowflow HD in monochorionic twins with twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome before and during fetoscopic laser ablation.
summary:
Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) affects monochorionic multiple pregnancies. Approximately 10–15% of monochorionic twins develop TTTS, which typically occurs between the 16th and 26th weeks of gestation. Monochorionic means that the fetuses share a placenta, and in virtually all cases, there are vascular connections between the umbilical circulations on the placental surface. Three different types of anastomoses have been described: arteriovenous, arteriarterial, and venovenous. As a result, an imbalance in blood volume between the two fetuses is possible. The exact cause of TTTS is not yet fully understood, but the number, type, and caliber of the anastomoses appear to determine the risk. Timely prenatal diagnosis of TTTS is essential for a good perinatal outcome. On ultrasound, a marked discrepancy in amniotic fluid volume is evident. The recipient twin exhibits polyhydramnios with a deepest pocket of at least 8 cm before the 20th week of gestation and over 10 cm after the 20th week of gestation. In contrast, the donor twin exhibits oligohydramnios (< 2 cm deepest pocket) to anhydramnios, and due to the tight-fitting amniotic membrane and the increased amniotic fluid of the co-twin, the donor twin becomes fixed to the wall of the uterus (stuck twin).
If left untreated, severe twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) leads to intrauterine death, miscarriage, or extreme preterm birth in 80–90% of cases. Laser ablation of placental vascular anastomoses is an established treatment method and the therapy of choice to stop the chronic imbalance in blood flow between the fetuses. 
To ablate as many anastomoses as possible during fetoscopic laser ablation, it is necessary to position the trocar at a site on the maternal abdomen during the laser procedure from which the entire vascular equator can be reached with the instruments. However, since there is currently no method to visualize this area prior to fetoscopic laser ablation, there is a risk that the trocar will be misplaced, thereby preventing the laser ablation from being performed completely.

interventions.name: This study will be the first to use Slowflow HD to visualize the placental vascular equator in monochorionic twins with TTTS.
